author: Mark Atwood
text:
[2026-05-11 scope decision] Confirmed with Mark in interactive triage session: option (b) single coordinated commit across all 6 sibling extension-client crates.

Title shape: `refactor(*-client): lift input parameter structs to lib root for canonical-template consistency`

Scope:
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/lib.rs — add missing input struct re-exports
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/lib.rs — add ~27 input struct re-exports (worst diverger)
- crate-jmap-contacts-client/src/lib.rs — add missing input struct re-exports
- crate-jmap-filenode-client/src/lib.rs — add missing input struct re-exports
- crate-jmap-sharing-client/src/lib.rs — add all input struct re-exports
- crate-jmap-tasks-client/src/lib.rs — add all input struct re-exports

Out of scope (do NOT touch in this sweep):
- crate-jmap-mail-client (the canonical oracle)
- `#[non_exhaustive]` divergence on chat-client's input structs (separate axis; file a follow-up bead if wanted)

Implementation method per sibling: enumerate input structs via `rg "^pub struct .*(Input|Params|Patch|Change|Created)" crate-jmap-{sibling}-client/src/methods/`, then add each to the lib.rs `pub use` list following the canonical jmap-mail-client pattern.

Rationale for single-commit over per-sibling PRs (option a from earlier triage):
1. Cookie-cutter validation works best with all 6 visible side-by-side.
2. Purely additive — no SemVer break, no public-type removal. Same risk profile in one PR or six.
3. Cuts a P3 epic candidate from the backlog before it lingers.

Removing `human` label. Ready to claim as a single multi-crate refactor bead.
